title: A Motor Neuron Is a Combination

scenes.visual: Title: A Motor Neuron Is a Combination. Preview a spinal cord, a motor neuron and its axon reaching muscle.

scenes.tts: A motor neuron is built by combinations of transcription factors acting in stages. The code first makes a motor neuron. Then it helps decide which muscle its axon will reach. That is why making a motor neuron is only part of the story. Follow the code from a stripe in the neural tube to a neuron connected to muscle.
scenes.narration: A motor neuron is built by combinations of transcription factors acting in stages. The code first makes a motor neuron. Then it helps decide which muscle its axon will reach. That is why making a motor neuron is only part of the story. Follow the code from a stripe in the neural tube to a neuron connected to muscle.

scenes.visual: Introduce a sequence: progenitor stripe → motor-neuron identity → column and pool → axon trajectory → muscle. Highlight the changing transcription-factor combination at each stage. Show target choice as the payoff, without implying that the code acts alone.

scenes.tts: Sonic hedgehog sets up a gradient across the neural tube. Progenitors read their position in it. One stripe, p M N, makes motor neurons. Its dividing cells carry Olig two. Around the final division, the cell turns on a new set.
scenes.narration: Sonic hedgehog sets up a gradient across the neural tube. Progenitors read their position in it. One stripe, pMN, makes motor neurons. Its dividing cells carry Olig2. Around the final division, the cell turns on a new set.
scenes.caption: Sonic hedgehog sets up a gradient across the neural tube. Progenitors read their position in it. One stripe, pMN, makes motor neurons. Its dividing cells carry Olig2. Around the final division, the cell turns on a new set.
scenes.visual: Show the Shh gradient and stacked progenitor domains. Highlight pMN and an Olig2-positive dividing progenitor; follow one daughter as it differentiates.

scenes.tts: Islet one or its relative Islet two, L H X three, and M N X one mark the newly differentiated motor neuron. But a marker is not a unique label. L H X three also appears in neighbouring V two interneurons. Its partners change its output.
scenes.narration: Isl1 or its relative Isl2, Lhx3, and Mnx1 mark the newly differentiated motor neuron. But a marker is not a unique label. Lhx3 also appears in neighbouring V2 interneurons. Its partners change its output.
scenes.caption: Isl1 or its relative Isl2, Lhx3, and Mnx1 mark the newly differentiated motor neuron. But a marker is not a unique label. Lhx3 also appears in neighbouring V2 interneurons. Its partners change its output.
scenes.visual: Show a postmitotic motor neuron with Isl1/or Isl2, Lhx3 and Mnx1 labels. Place a V2 interneuron beside it with the same Lhx3 colour. Do not present Lhx3 as a permanent marker in every motor-neuron subtype.

scenes.tts: In chick, L H X three without Islet one binds N L I and promotes V two interneuron genes. Add Islet one, and a different complex promotes motor-neuron genes. The combination matters.
scenes.narration: In chick, Lhx3 without Isl1 binds NLI and promotes V2 interneuron genes. Add Isl1, and a different complex promotes motor-neuron genes. The combination matters.
scenes.caption: In chick, Lhx3 without Isl1 binds NLI and promotes V2 interneuron genes. Add Isl1, and a different complex promotes motor-neuron genes. The combination matters.
scenes.visual: Use a compact chick-labelled comparison: Lhx3 with NLI → V2 genes; with Isl1 present → Isl1-containing motor-neuron complex → motor-neuron genes. Retain NLI in the motor-neuron assembly. Use simple chips, without binding sockets, C-terminal tails or a structural close-up.

scenes.tts: Delete Islet one in mouse, and motor neurons are not generated. Delete M N X one, and they form but transiently show V two features, with disordered columns and axons. Making a cell and maintaining its identity are different jobs.
scenes.narration: Delete Isl1 in mouse, and motor neurons are not generated. Delete Mnx1, and they form but transiently show V2 features, with disordered columns and axons. Making a cell and maintaining its identity are different jobs.
scenes.caption: Delete Isl1 in mouse, and motor neurons are not generated. Delete Mnx1, and they form but transiently show V2 features, with disordered columns and axons. Making a cell and maintaining its identity are different jobs.
scenes.visual: Two mouse deletion rows: Isl1 deletion → motor neurons not generated; Mnx1 deletion → motor neurons generated, then transient V2 features and disordered columns/projections. Keep this necessity evidence distinct from the preceding chick gain-of-function experiment.

scenes.tts: Now, which motor neuron? Hox proteins record position along the cord. With Fox P one, they assign columns and pools. The lateral motor column supplies limb muscles. A pool supplies one muscle. Delete Fox P one in mouse, and motor neurons still form. But limb and autonomic column identities fail. In the limb, axons appear to choose paths and muscles at random.

A pool supplies one muscle. Delete Foxp1 in mouse, and motor neurons still form. But limb and autonomic column identities fail. In the limb, axons appear to choose paths and muscles at random.

A pool supplies one muscle. Delete Foxp1 in mouse, and motor neurons still form. But limb and autonomic column identities fail. In the limb, axons appear to choose paths and muscles at random.
scenes.visual: Show Hox profiles along the cord, then FoxP1-dependent column and pool identities. Label lateral motor column → limb muscles and pool → one muscle. In a mouse Foxp1-deletion comparison retain motor neurons but show failed limb/autonomic identities and apparently random limb trajectories/targets. Avoid suggesting that all columns require FoxP1.

scenes.tts: The code also reaches the axon. Lateral cells of the limb column express L H X one, which ensures a dorsal trajectory in the limb. Without it, their axons lose that preference. Eph receptors and ephrins are part of the guidance machinery. Identity helps set the route.
scenes.narration: The code also reaches the axon. Lateral cells of the limb column express Lhx1, which ensures a dorsal trajectory in the limb. Without it, their axons lose that preference. Eph receptors and ephrins are part of the guidance machinery. Identity helps set the route.
scenes.caption: The code also reaches the axon. Lateral cells of the limb column express Lhx1, which ensures a dorsal trajectory in the limb. Without it, their axons lose that preference. Eph receptors and ephrins are part of the guidance machinery. Identity helps set the route.
scenes.visual: Zoom to lateral LMC neurons expressing Lhx1 and trace their axons dorsally into the limb. Compare loss of Lhx1: the dorsal preference disappears. Show Eph receptors/ephrins as part of a broader set of guidance cues, not the only mechanism.

scenes.tts: Use that developmental logic in a dish. In mouse embryonic stem cells, retinoic acid promotes spinal character. A Hedgehog agonist pushes cells toward p M N. Motor neurons follow. This basic protocol gives mostly medial motor column cells. Making one named pool remains harder. The code can build motor neurons, but its fine detail is still incomplete.
scenes.narration: Use that developmental logic in a dish. In mouse embryonic stem cells, retinoic acid promotes spinal character. A Hedgehog agonist pushes cells toward pMN. Motor neurons follow. This basic protocol gives mostly medial motor column cells. Making one named pool remains harder. The code can build motor neurons, but its fine detail is still incomplete.

This basic protocol gives mostly medial motor column cells. Making one named pool remains harder. The code can build motor neurons, but its fine detail is still incomplete.
scenes.visual: Show mouse embryonic stem cells → spinal progenitors → Mnx1-positive motor neurons. Label retinoic acid: relatively rostral hindbrain/cervical patterning; Hedgehog agonist: ventral/pMN patterning. Label the basic protocol as biased toward medial motor column. End with an unresolved named-pool target; do not depict muscle synapses forming in the dish.
End card: A staged transcription-factor code builds identity and helps specify connections. Hold the cord-to-muscle overview.
